title: service-degradation-liability-quick-sandbox
content:
Notes to self - scratchpad for service-degradation / partial-outage liability language and negotiation play.

Context: we sell hosted API + Dedicated + Private. Customers sometimes ask for granular SLAs beyond uptime (e.g., latency tiers, per-model availability, partial degradation when a model falls back). Need concise, negotiable fallback language and clear caps. This is messy in practice — we want consistent rebuttals and optional concessions.

Top-level goals (priority order):
1) Limit financial exposure (cap at fees paid; prefer short cure windows).
2) Preserve operational flexibility (allow measured rollbacks, fallback to compatible model variants).
3) Tie remedies to observable signals (latency p99, error-rate, model-fallback events) with clear measurement sources.
4) Make credits predictable and small enough not to be catastrophic.

Key negotiation talking points (quick scripts):
- Customer: "We need compensation when the model is degraded."
  Response: "We can do defined service credits tied to documented SLO metrics — that keeps things predictable for both sides. For catastrophic loss we can talk about one-time remediation support but not open-ended indemnity."
- Customer: "We want unlimited liability for degraded outputs."
  Response: "We can accept narrowly tailored financial remedies for verified platform outages, not for model quality disputes or downstream business loss. For output-quality regressions we propose an eval/regression play (prompt set + re-run window) rather than cash."

Signals/metrics to accept as triggers (recommended):
- Platform availability: per-region API availability measured at our edge proxies (p95 availability window)
- Serving degradation: sustained token-level error-rate > X% for N minutes OR sustained model-fallback > Y% of requests
- Latency SLO breaches: p99 latency > threshold for >M minutes
- Model quality regressions: only tied to our verified rollout tests / customer-provided prompt set and statistically significant delta

Suggested credit structure (simple, defensible):
- Minor degradation (e.g., single-region p99 breach or latency spike lasting 5-30 minutes): 5% of daily pro-rated invoice for each distinct incident up to 30% monthly cap
- Major degradation (multi-region outage or sustained failure > 2 hours): 20% of monthly pro-rated fees for that service month, capped at 50% of that month's fees
- Absolute cap across all remedies: no more than 100% of fees paid in the 12-month period tied to that service (or preferably 50% if we want tight cap)
- No credits for: downstream business loss, reputation, aggregated quality drift, or incidents caused by customer misconfiguration or third-party infra (unless we control the dependency)

Draft redline snippets (plain language to propose) — keep short and negotiable:
- "Customer Remedies: If Redwood fails to meet the Availability SLO for a Service as measured by Redwood's monitoring for a continuous period exceeding two (2) hours, Customer may request a Service Credit equal to twenty percent (20%) of the pro-rated fees paid for that Service for the affected month. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any unavailability of the Service."
- "For transient degradations under two (2) hours, Redwood may, at its discretion, apply a Service Credit of five percent (5%) of the pro-rated fees for the affected day. Multiple transient events in a single month are subject to the monthly caps set forth herein."
- "All Service Credit calculations are determined by Redwood based on Redwood's monitoring data. Customer may request debug logs and telemetry relevant to any credit claim. Parties will meet within ten (10) business days to validate claims. Approved Service Credits will be applied against subsequent invoices; they are non-refundable and do not constitute a waiver of any other rights."

Optional concessions to use as negotiation levers (ordered low to high cost):
- Lower minor incident credit from 5% to 3% in exchange for extended telemetry retention (30 -> 90 days) so customer can self-validate
- Offer a one-time remediation SLA (engineering support hours) in lieu of partial credits for first incident over X threshold
- For high-tier enterprise (Dedicated): increase major incident credit to 25% and raise monthly cap to 60% if customer commits to annual reserved capacity and an operational runbook with Redwood

Areas to push back hard on (non-starters):
- Unlimited or uncapped consequential damages tied to degraded or incorrect model outputs
- Remedies that allow customer to withhold payments beyond simple offset of credits (no mutual set-off except as described)
- Requirements that we keep multiple cold standbys for every model in every region (operationally unfeasible)

Measurement & evidence (practical notes):
- Always require that triggers be based on Redwood's monitoring / RBAC-extracted telemetry. If customer insists on third-party monitoring, propose a neutral arbiter or fix a single mutual telemetry snapshot mechanism (file hash of logs).
- For model-quality claims: require a reproducible prompt set and a run window — we re-run against pinned model version and compare. Define statistical test (e.g., paired t-test / exact-binary delta threshold).

Fallback language (important for hosted offering & Dedicated):
- "Redwood may, when capacity or quality constraints occur, route Customer requests to a compatible model variant or degrade to a best-effort tier. Redwood will notify Customer and publish the fallback period in the console. Fallbacks are not a breach if Redwood continues to provide an endpoint and documents the deviation."

Short risk matrix for sales/legal to remember (deal triage):
- Small startup, low spend (<$5k/month): push standard credit cap (20% monthly) and no extra telemetry
- Mid-market ($5k-$50k): consider customization: add remediation hours or telemetry retention in exchange for modest weekly reporting
- Enterprise (> $50k+/mo): be prepared to trade higher caps for reserved capacity + longer notice + operational runbook + premium support fees

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final absolute cap: 50% vs 100% of 12-month fees? (ops prefers 50%)
- Formalize regression-test language for model-quality claims (who owns the prompt set, acceptance thresholds)
- Bake into contract templates: one short clause for Hosted, one for Dedicated (different fallbacks, measurement sources)
- Add a small clause about Force Majeure including dependency failures (major cloud provider) — make sure it excludes cases where failure is within Redwood's control (supply chain / provisioning errors)

Quick checklist before sharing with sales:
- [ ] Pick absolute cap (recommendation: 50% 12-mo for hosted; 75% 12-mo for Dedicated with reserved capacity)
- [ ] Draft concise fallback clause for Dedicated vs Hosted
- [ ] Send to infra + SRE for feasibility of telemetry retention ask
- [ ] Add sample negotiation bullets to sales playbook (email + 2–3 speak lines)

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Could we offer a "degradation insurance" add-on: small extra % fee that increases caps / reduces cure windows for customers who purchase it? (monetize risk transfer)
- Consider SLA page in Console (self-serve claims) — reduces back-and-forth and provides audit log for incidents)

End of scratchpad. Keep short snippets above; will iterate into clean clause sets for templates.

Notes to self: save two versions (strict-limited-cap and enterprise-flex) and tag in Confluence (CON-1423) before next legal review.
